inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The zero-order elimination plot: y-axis 'Drug plasma concentration' (with ↑), x-axis 'Time (h)'. Cp falls in a straight LINE — the elimination rate (=slope) is constant at 2 U/h regardless of Cp (the graph labels 2 U/h twice along the line). Horizontal dashed guides mark the successive halvings (4 → 2 → 1 → 0.5) and the three half-life intervals are bracketed beneath the x-axis: 'First t1/2 >', 'Second t1/2 >', 'Third t1/2' — each successive interval is SHORTER. The graph's rule annotation reads 'Time of t1/2 ↑ as concentration ↑' (half-life is NOT constant in zero-order elimination; it lengthens as concentration rises). A vector figure (no raster).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the zero-order panel of the EliminationOfDrugsMap)

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The first-order elimination plot: y-axis 'Drug plasma concentration' (with ↑), x-axis 'Time (h)'. Cp falls on an exponential CURVE — the elimination rate (=slope) is labeled at four successive positions (4 U/h, 2 U/h, 1 U/h, 0.5 U/h) and FALLS in proportion to the concentration. The three half-life intervals are bracketed beneath the x-axis: 'First t1/2 =', 'Second t1/2 =', 'Third t1/2' — every interval is EQUAL. The graph's rule annotation reads 'Time of t1/2 is constant as concentration ↑' (half-life is constant in first-order elimination). A vector figure (no raster).
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the first-order panel of the EliminationOfDrugsMap)

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The zero-order vs first-order comparison rows
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The two comparison rows printed under the 'Elimination of drugs' header. Zero-order row: 'Rate of elimination is constant regardless of Cp (ie, constant amount of drug eliminated per unit time). Cp ↓ linearly with time. Examples of drugs—Phenytoin, Ethanol, and Aspirin (at high or toxic concentrations → ↑ salicylate saturation → zero-order elimination).' with the side note 'Capacity-limited elimination.' First-order row: 'Rate of first-order elimination is directly proportional to the drug concentration (ie, constant fraction of drug eliminated per unit time). Cp ↓ exponentially with time. Applies to most drugs.' with the side note 'Flow-dependent elimination.' Pure text, no figures.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (the comparison table strip inside the EliminationOfDrugsMap) + blocks[1] and blocks[2] the table blocks carried verbatim

inventory.visualPurpose: The PEA margin mnemonic (the page's own zero-order drug mnemonic)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The mnemonic printed beside the zero-order row: 'A PEA is round, shaped like the “0” in zero-order.' — coding the three zero-order example drugs Phenytoin, Ethanol, Aspirin (a pea is round like the numeral 0). A short attributed phrase carried in the evidence layer and the KYP mnemonic layer; the KYP visual renders its OWN original callout design around the phrase (the three additional codes — AMOUNT vs FRACTION, LINE vs CURVE, CAPACITY vs FLOW — are KYP-original).
